quick: 0.5 mL subcutaneously; two doses 4-8 weeks apart (>=13 years)
Contraindicated; avoid pregnancy for 1 month after vaccination
Use with caution; benefit usually outweighs theoretical risk
summary: Varicella virus vaccine, live (Oka/Merck strain) is a live attenuated vaccine that induces protective immunity against varicella (chickenpox). It is given subcutaneously - two doses for children 12 months and older, adolescents, and adults. As a live vaccine it is contraindicated in pregnancy and significant immunosuppression. It provides durable protection and substantially reduces disease severity even in breakthrough cases.
indications: Active immunization for the prevention of varicella (chickenpox) in individuals 12 months of age and older

dosage.n: 1st at 12-15 months, 2nd at 4-6 years (minimum 3 months apart)

admin: Administer subcutaneously, preferably in the outer aspect of the upper arm (deltoid) or anterolateral thigh
Reconstitute only with the supplied diluent; use immediately (within 30 minutes) after reconstitution
Do not inject intravascularly or intramuscularly
Do not mix with other vaccines in the same syringe
Maintain the cold chain; protect the lyophilized vaccine from light
moa: The vaccine contains live, attenuated varicella-zoster virus (Oka/Merck strain). Subcutaneous administration produces a controlled subclinical infection that stimulates humoral (anti-VZV antibody) and cell-mediated immune responses, generating immunologic memory. On subsequent natural exposure, this primed immunity prevents or attenuates varicella disease.

absolute: History of anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction to the vaccine, gelatin, or neomycin
Primary or acquired immunodeficiency (e.g., advanced symptomatic HIV, leukemia, lymphoma, blood dyscrasias)
relative: Recent receipt of immune globulin or blood products (defer vaccination)
Family history of congenital/hereditary immunodeficiency until competence established
Concurrent salicylate (aspirin) therapy - avoid for 6 weeks after vaccination
monitor: Avoidance of contact with high-risk susceptible individuals if rash develops

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. The effects on fetal development are unknown; do not vaccinate pregnant women. Avoid pregnancy for at least 1 month (some guidance: 3 months) following vaccination.
lact: It is not known whether vaccine virus is excreted in human milk; wild-type VZV is not. Use with caution in breastfeeding women - the benefit of maternal immunity generally outweighs the theoretical risk.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for hepatic impairment.

major: Immunosuppressants / high-dose corticosteroids (impaired immune response and risk of disseminated vaccine infection - contraindicated)
Immune globulin / blood products (may blunt response - separate by appropriate interval)
moderate: Salicylates (avoid for 6 weeks post-vaccination due to reported Reye syndrome association)
Other live vaccines (give same day or separate by >=4 weeks)
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently affect tuberculin skin test reactivity - defer TST or perform on the day of vaccination

common: Varicella-like rash (localized or generalized, usually mild)
serious: Disseminated vaccine-strain varicella in immunocompromised recipients
rare: Herpes zoster from vaccine strain (much less common/milder than wild-type)
Encephalitis, ataxia, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (very rare, causal relationship not established)
emergency: Disseminated varicella infection in an immunocompromised host

monitoring: Observe for immediate allergic reactions after administration (have epinephrine available)
Monitor for vaccine-related rash within 1-3 weeks
Advise avoidance of contact with high-risk susceptible persons (pregnant women, immunocompromised, neonates) if a rash develops
Confirm completion of the two-dose series
counsel: This vaccine prevents chickenpox; two doses are needed for full protection
Mild fever or a few chickenpox-like spots may appear in the weeks after vaccination
Avoid aspirin/salicylates for 6 weeks after vaccination
Avoid becoming pregnant for at least 1 month after vaccination
If a rash develops, avoid close contact with pregnant women, newborns, and people with weak immune systems
pk: Protective antibody develops over several weeks after vaccination
Peak immune response within weeks of the second dose
Not applicable (vaccine - induces durable immune memory)
Long-term protection (years to decades); two-dose schedule improves durability
Store frozen per product labeling; protect from light; use reconstituted vaccine within 30 minutes
pearls: Live attenuated vaccine - contraindicated in pregnancy and significant immunosuppression
Not listed in openFDA drug labels because it is a biologic (e.g., VARIVAX); source is the FDA package insert / CBER and ACIP recommendations
Avoid salicylates for 6 weeks after vaccination (theoretical Reye syndrome risk)
Two-dose schedule markedly reduces breakthrough varicella compared with a single dose
missed: If the second dose is delayed, give it as soon as feasible; the series does not need to be restarted. Follow the recommended minimum interval between doses.
overdose: Overdose is not clinically relevant for a single-dose vaccine; inadvertent administration of more than the recommended volume is managed with observation. Manage any hypersensitivity reaction supportively.
